newsitem.title: CHINA: Rhone-Poulenc to double China investment.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc to double China investment.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc SA is ready to more than double its $300 million China investment before 2005, as the local focus of the French pharmaceuticals and chemicals giant shifts to life-science products, company officials said on Friday.
Rhone-Poulenc expected to raise annual sales from China, Hong Kong and Taiwan to $1.0 billion before 2005 from $250 million in 1996, Vice Chairman Jean Marc Bruel said.

Up to $700 million in investment would be needed to achieve such revenues, and Rhone-Poulenc was already in the late stages of negotiations to set up 15 new joint ventures in China, Bruel told a news conference in Beijing.

Beijing had in the past favoured chemical and fibres ventures, but Rhone-Poulenc's focus in China would now begin to shift toward its main fields of pharmaceuticals and animal and plant health, said company Chairman Jean-Rene Fourtou.
"China now is...more open to the life sciences part than it was before," Fourtou said. "We think the new wave of starting ventures will be in life sciences."
Rhone-Poulenc currently has seven ventures in China to produce chemical products, as well as four to make fibres and polymers and three involved in pharmaceuticals.

The French group expected to agree on a $90 million-joint venture to produce Regent, its low-dose rice insecticide, in China's eastern Zhejiang province, said General Delegate for Greater China Aldo Salvador.
"We expect to sign the deal in December," Salvador said, but declined to give further details.

Greater China -- the mainland along with Hong Kong and Taiwan -- was at the heart of Rhone-Poulenc's efforts to raise Asia-Pacific revenues to account for 15 percent of total company sales by 2000, up from 9.7 percent in 1996, Fourtou said.

During a visit to China by French President Jacques Chirac earlier this month, the company signed an $87.7 million joint venture agreement with a pesticide plant in the eastern city of Hangzhou to turn out plant protection products.
Rhone-Poulenc was to hold a 75 percent stake in the venture while the Hangzhou General Pesticides Plant took the remaining 25 percent, an official of the Chinese company said.

Rhone-Poulenc officials said the creation of a holding company to help overcome formidable distribution problems had helped to equip the French company to achieve its ambitious plans to raise Greater China sales to $750 million by 2000.
"Today, we have the necessary organisation to understand the complexities of China and to move forward," Salvador said.
